title: Mutual Aid Response Lag by Need Type
dataSources: Volunteer shifts (`community:shift`), donations (`community:donation`), mutual-aid requests (`community:mutualaid`), service ops (`community:impact`).
app: Community-service telemetry — food-bank shift logs, blood-donation records, and mutual-aid request maps — streamed to Splunk HEC via exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=community:mutualaid need_type=* requested_epoch=* first_response_epoch=*
| eval lag_hours=round((first_response_epoch-requested_epoch)/3600,1)
| stats avg(lag_hours) as avg_lag_hours, max(lag_hours) as worst_lag_hours by need_type
| sort - avg_lag_hours
description: Measures response lag by need type for mutual-aid requests.
value: Lag tracking shows which need type create the slowest handoffs, syncs, or review loops inside mutual-aid requests.
implementation: Capture the timestamps needed to compute `response lag` on `community:mutualaid` events and aggregate them by `need_type`.
visualization: Table of need type with average and worst response lag.
grandmaExplanation: It monitors how long things take for each need type so you can see where mutual-aid requests slows down.
